background_notes.fact: A real normed space V carries a metric d(x,y)=‖x−y‖, and hence an extended metric obtained by embedding its nonnegative real distances into [0,∞].

grounds.reason: V is the arbitrary real normed space declared before the applications in S001.

background_notes.justification: Norm definiteness gives d(x,y)=0 exactly when x=y; norm symmetry gives symmetry; the norm triangle inequality applied to (x−y)+(y−z) gives the distance triangle inequality. Embedding nonnegative real distances preserves these identities and inequalities.

background_notes.fact: For every natural m its canonical value in [0,∞] is strictly below ∞. If x∈[0,∞] and x≤m, then 0≤x<∞ and x is the canonical image of a unique nonnegative real; when m=0, x=0.

grounds.reason: finrank(V) has natural-number values, canonically embedded in [0,∞].

background_notes.justification: The extended nonnegative reals consist of the nonnegative real values and an additional greatest element ∞. A natural m embeds as its finite nonnegative real value. An element bounded above by m cannot be ∞ and therefore has a unique finite real representative. Zero is least; if x≤0, antisymmetry gives x=0.
